questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the roadway, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before hitting an obstacle. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel just before impact.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Never ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may show a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your fingers near the clutch and brake levers. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: When riding in a lane of traffic, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is best for all situations. Change your position based on changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds of distance when riding at night. It is harder to see and judge distances in the dark. You may need extra time to notice a vehicle stopping and to brake or avoid it.

questions.question: To be effective, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Not allow for eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Restrict your vision to the sides.

questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must be scratch-free, resist penetration, provide clear side vision, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, you should do everything EXCEPT:

options.text: Limit the distance traveled in a day.

questions.explanation: Dress to protect against wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and stop for a break every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants because you may crash when they wear off and fatigue hits suddenly.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should stay just behind the leader. This keeps them from falling behind and allows experienced riders to watch them.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle or a motorcycle with a sidecar, why should you not ride too far to the right of your lane?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar extends to the right side of a motorcycle. If you ride too far right, the sidecar can run off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the right rear wheel can also leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: What is the best riding formation for a group of motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way to ride in a group. Switch to single-file when turning, riding through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog calmly. Then accelerate to leave it behind. If you see a larger animal, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
Stay in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: How should you swerve to avoid a hazard?

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the direction opposite of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve, apply light pressure to the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press right to recover. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: How should you apply the front brake?

options.text: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
Grab at the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever firmly with all four fingers. Apply increasing pressure smoothly.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop your motorcycle?

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line stop, apply brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight moves forward, use more front brake and less rear brake. Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat on a motorcycle. Instead, you will notice a change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?

options.text: Move your shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by closing the throttle and applying the brakes if needed.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles can ride in a staggered formation, but three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this. Three-wheel motorcycles must travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the extra weight.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of a lane.
Ride in the center portion of a lane.
Give dirty looks to drivers entering your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, which action should you avoid?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more slippery than other road surfaces.
